To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sustained neuronal activity downregulates the expression and function of the neuron-specific KCC2 cotransporter.
1) Sustained interictal-like neuronal activity in hippocampi downregulates the neuron-specific KCC2 mRNA/protein expression in CA1, which leads to reduced neuronal Cl- extruding capacity.
BDNF, acting via the TrkB receptor, downregulates neuronal expression of the K-Cl cottransporter, KCC, which leads to an impairment of GABA-mediated fast hyperpolarizing inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of activity-dependent changes in KCC expression and their role in the regulation of GABAergic inhibition.
the role of KCC2 in the regulation of neuronal activity.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the neuron-specific KCC2 cotransporter, which is a key component of the inhibitory GABAergic system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

BDNF-TrkB signaling downregulates K-Cl cotranporter KCC2 via Shc/FRs-2 and PLCγ signaling pathways, which leads to the reduction in the capacity of neurons to extrude Cl- and to the loss of GABAergic fast inhibition.
KCC2 downregulation is a common phenomenon, and is mediated by a complex signaling pathway, which is triggered by BDNF.
the activity-dependent downregulation of the neuron-specific KCl cotransporter KCC-2, which is mediated by endogenously released BDNF, represents a general early response to neuronal injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the BDNF/TrkB/FRS2/PLCγ/cAMP response element-binding (CREB) signaling pathway regulates KCC2 expression and activity-dependent downregulation of neuronal KCC2 expression may contribute to various kinds of neuronal plasticity and neuronal injury.
BDNF/TrkB/FRS-1/2/PLCγ/cAMP response element-binding proteins signaling pathway mediates downregulation of neuronal KCC2 expression, which may contribute to the development of epilepsy.

the down-regulation of KCC is a general early response to various kinds of neuronal traumas, and this response is mediated by BDNF acting via TrkB, with Shc/FR-2 and PLCγ-cAMP response element-binding proteins signaling cascades.
The main takeaway from our work is that
KCC2 expression is down-regulated during seizure activity.

KCC2 is a dynamic, plastic molecule, and that its expression can be modulated by activity, and by BDNF, in a way that may be involved in various types of neuronal plasticity, and in various forms of neuronal trauma.
the activity-dependent downregulation of the neuron-specific KCC2 is a mechanism that can be used to modulate GABAergic inhibition.
